output:
# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Procurement | **From:** Legal | **Re:** Calyx Workforce Software – ShiftPilot MSA (Order Form: 3 yrs, $180k/yr + $60k implementation; total contract value $600k)

---

## 1. Bottom line: don't sign yet

Not signable Friday as drafted. Four reasons, in order:

1. **No BAA.** Section 7.3 points to Exhibit C, which is blank. ShiftPilot ingests patient names, units and acuity scores – PHI. Importing the census without an executed BAA puts Riverbend in breach of HIPAA on day one, regardless of what the MSA says.
2. **The liability cap is ~$45,000 – possibly $0.** "Fees" (§1.7) means subscription fees only, so three months = $45,000; the $60k implementation fee is excluded. Worse, the cap is fees *paid* in the preceding three months – if we prepay annually, the cap is $0 for nine months of every year. Playbook floor is $240,000 (12 months of all fees in year one) with a $540,000 super-cap (3× annual fees) for data breaches. The only carve-out references §10.4, which does not exist, so *nothing* sits outside the cap – including indemnities.
3. **The indemnity runs the wrong way.** §10.2 has Riverbend indemnifying Calyx for "any claim arising from Customer Data" – which on its face includes a patient class action caused by Calyx's own breach. §9.2 then excludes breach notification, credit monitoring and loss of data – the exact costs we would incur.
4. **Lock-in.** Three-year auto-renewals at up to 9% with 120 days' notice; export costs extra and data is deleted at day 30.

We can sign Friday only if Calyx accepts points 1–3 in Section 3 below in a signed amendment. Otherwise, one week's slip is cheap insurance.

---

## 2. Issues table

| Clause | Issue | Risk | Proposed redline | Acceptable fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **7.3 / Ex. C** | BAA "intentionally omitted"; no HIPAA coverage for PHI | **High** | Attach Riverbend's standard BAA as Exhibit C, executed concurrently; add: "No PHI will be transmitted until Exhibit C is executed. In any conflict concerning PHI, Exhibit C controls." | Calyx's BAA if it meets 45 CFR 164.504(e), includes 5-business-day incident notice, and is signed before go-live (not before MSA signature) |
| **1.7 / 9.1** | Cap = 3 months' subscription fees paid (~$45k, possibly $0); excludes implementation; carve-out to phantom §10.4 | **High** | "…shall not exceed the greater of (a) $240,000 and (b) all fees (including implementation and professional-services fees) paid *or payable* in the 12 months preceding the claim. Excluded from this cap: (i) indemnification obligations under §10; (ii) gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud. Vendor's liability for breach of §7, Exhibit C or confidentiality is capped at 3× annual subscription fees ($540,000)." | General cap of 12 months' fees payable ($180k) if implementation fee treated separately; super-cap of $540k that also absorbs indemnities (i.e., indemnities inside super-cap, not general cap) |
| **9.2** | Excludes loss of data, notification and credit-monitoring costs | **High** | "Section 9.2 does not apply to Excluded Claims. Costs of breach notification, credit monitoring, forensic investigation, data restoration and regulatory fines (to the extent lawful) are direct damages." | Keep exclusion but expressly deem notification/credit-monitoring/restoration costs direct damages |
| **10.1–10.3** | No vendor data-breach indemnity; Customer indemnifies Vendor for any claim "arising from Customer Data"; §10.3 closes the door | **High** | Add §10.4: "Vendor will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims and regulatory actions arising from Vendor's breach of §7, Exhibit C or a Security Incident." Narrow §10.2 to "claims that Customer Data *as provided by Customer* infringes third-party rights or was unlawfully provided, except to the extent caused by Vendor." | Vendor breach indemnity limited to third-party claims (not regulatory actions), inside the $540k super-cap |
| **8.1** | 99.5% on "commercially reasonable efforts"; unlimited maintenance on 24h notice; credits sole remedy | **Medium** | "Vendor will make the Service available 99.9% each month. Scheduled maintenance limited to 8 hours/month, outside 06:00–22:00 ET, on 5 business days' notice. If Vendor misses the commitment in any 2 consecutive months or 3 of any 6, Customer may terminate for cause and receive a refund of prepaid fees. Credits are otherwise the sole remedy." | 99.7% with the chronic-failure termination right; scheduled maintenance capped at 12 hours/month |
| **12.2** | 3-yr auto-renewal, 120 days' notice, 9% uplift | **Medium** | "Renews for successive one-year terms unless either party gives 60 days' notice. Vendor will send written renewal reminder 90–120 days before each term end. Renewal fee increase capped at the lesser of 3% or CPI-U." | 1-year terms, 90 days' notice, cap of lesser of 5% or CPI, plus the mandatory vendor reminder |
| **13.1** | NY law (good) but exclusive venue in Wilmington, DE | **Medium** | "…exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York." | Non-exclusive jurisdiction; or each party sues only in the other's home forum (makes Calyx come to NY to sue us) |
| **14.3** | Deletion at 30 days; export at PS rates | **Medium** | "For 60 days after termination Vendor will make all Customer Data available for self-service export in CSV/JSON (or other mutually agreed standard format) at no charge, then delete and certify deletion, subject to retention required by law or Exhibit C." | 45 days, one free full export, self-service portal; PS rates only for custom formats |

---

## 3. Five points to win on Friday's call (priority order)

1. **BAA signed, or no PHI.** Non-negotiable. Exhibit C executed with the MSA; BAA controls on conflicts. If Calyx cannot produce a compliant BAA by Friday, we don't sign Friday.
2. **Cap and exclusions.** $240k general cap on *all* fees paid or payable; $540k super-cap for data-protection breaches; fix the phantom §10.4 cross-reference; carve notification/credit-monitoring/data-restoration costs out of §9.2. Frame it to Calyx: their current drafting leaves them exposed to *uncapped* indemnity ambiguity too – a clean structure helps both sides.
3. **Indemnity direction.** Add the vendor breach indemnity (§10.4) and narrow §10.2. We cannot indemnify a vendor for its own breach of our patients' data.
4. **Renewal.** One-year renewals, 60 days' notice, 3%/CPI cap, vendor reminder notice. Trade: we can accept 90 days' notice if they take 1-year terms and the 3% cap.
5. **Exit and SLA package.** Free standard-format export, 60-day retention, 99.9% with chronic-failure termination. Venue to New York County is our opener here; if Calyx digs in, trade venue for the exit terms – NY law is already secured.

---

## 4. The two statutes

**GOL §5-1401(1) – helps, modestly.** The aggregate contract value ($600,000) clears the $250,000 threshold, so the New York choice of law in §13.1 is enforceable even if Calyx has no New York nexus and even in a Delaware court. Note what it does *not* do: it secures governing law, not forum. The companion provision (§5-1402, not excerpted) gives access to New York courts only for contracts of $1 million or more with a New York forum consent – we qualify on neither. Venue must be fixed by negotiation.

**GOL §5-903(2) – a backstop, not a plan.** If it applies, Calyx's 3-year auto-renewal is unenforceable unless Calyx serves certified-mail or personal notice 15–30 days before our 120-day non-renewal deadline. Two cautions: (i) the statute covers contracts "for service, maintenance or repair to or for any real or personal property"; courts have applied it mainly to tangible-asset service contracts (equipment, alarm systems), and a SaaS subscription to our operations rather than our property may fall outside it; (ii) a Delaware court applying NY law may read it narrowly. Use it as leverage on the call – "New York policy disfavours surprise renewals; put the reminder in the contract" – and draft §12.2 to mirror its mechanics. Separately, calendar the non-renewal deadline (currently ~8 months before each term end) regardless of outcome.
